name: card
what: The finished box: a surface with border, radius, built-in padding and a gap between its children, plus an optional coloured status edge.
render: import { div, h3, p } from '/app.js'; div.c('card', () => { h3('Title'); p('A card needs no extra CSS.'); });
notes: Count is files whose class strings mention card, including hand-rolled ones. Reserves a 3px inline-start edge always, so it is 3px narrower inside than .surface. · The ui/card page still teaches 'surface pad flex v gap', the older form the .card word replaced; the two disagree on gap (0.5*--gap vs --gap). · Count is files with c("card. The 3px edge is always reserved. framework.css:456 says 180 hand-rolled card classes were the reason .card exists.

name: surface
what: The bare box look (background, border, radius) with no padding; the base every component adds its own padding to.
render: import { div, p } from '/app.js'; div.c('surface pad', () => p('A surface plus a pad.'));
notes: 'surface pad' (132 files) does the same job as .card but pads with --pad, not --pad-card, and has no gap rhythm or edge: twin with different spacing. · Twin of .card: forgetting the second word gives an unpadded box, the trap .card was made to remove. Count is files with c("surface.

name: wash
what: A quiet filled background, used for placeholders, media areas and count chips.
render: import { div } from '/app.js'; div.c('wash pad', 'A washed band');
notes: wash and tint are two background words for near-identical jobs. · Class was once missing while token existed and painted nothing silently. · --tint once had no class and painted nothing silently (framework.css comment after line 503).

name: pad
what: Padding word: gives any box the page-region padding.
render: import { div } from '/app.js'; div.c('surface pad', 'Padded');
notes: Not a box itself; listed because it is the spacing half of surface pad.

name: bleed
what: Layout word: a block on a five-track page that takes the full width, edge to edge, including the page inset.
bleeds: yes: spans all five grid tracks
notes: Rule lives in the theme layer (page-column-prose > .bleed); not standalone drawable, needs a standard page. Count includes other 'bleed' uses (e.g. ai css).
undrawable: It is a layout word, not a box: it only widens a direct child of a five-track page, so it has nothing to draw on its own.

name: stat tile

notes: Template only, no export. Same 'label + value' box is hand-built elsewhere. · Built from utility words, not .card: another spelling of a small padded box.

name: agents strip chip
what: A chip for one running or idle agent; on = selected.
render: import { div, span, p, a, button, input, textarea, label, details, summary, progress, icon } from '/app.js'; div.c('v3-agents-rows', () => { button.c('v3-agents-row on').attr('type', 'button').text('catalog · minion · working'); button.c('v3-agents-row').attr('type', 'button').text('census-a · minion · idle'); });
notes: Reads an agent host stream, not standalone.

name: view button
what: A small toggle button in the v3 toolbar (sort / view).
render: import { button } from '/app.js'; button.c('v3-view-btn on', 'Grid').attr('type', 'button');
notes: Three toolbar buttons that do the same thing. · Needs a panel item.

name: undo toast
what: A bar with a message and Undo, at the bottom of the board.
render: import { div, span, p, a, button, input, textarea, label, details, summary, progress, icon } from '/app.js'; div.c('v3-toast card', () => { span.c('v3-toast-msg', 'Card cleared'); button.c('v3-toast-undo').attr('type', 'button').text('Undo'); });

name: ask answer buttons
what: The row of option buttons that answers an ask from a v3 card.
render: import { div, span, p, a, button, input, textarea, label, details, summary, progress, icon } from '/app.js'; div.c('v3-ask v3-ask-options', () => { div.c('card', () => p('Option A')); div.c('card', () => p('Option B')); });

name: panel properties row
what: A labelled knob (range, output) in the properties region.
render: import { div, span, p, a, button, input, textarea, label, details, summary, progress, icon } from '/app.js'; div.c('panel-props', () => div.c('panel-props-row', () => { span('gap'); input().attr('type', 'range').ac('panel-knob-range'); span.c('panel-knob-out', '12'); }));
notes: Needs a focused panel.

name: panel template block
what: A ready-made content block dropped into a panel: stat, clock, rail, contents list, brand.
render: import { templates } from '/framework/ext/Panel/templates.js'; templates.toc.draw();
notes: Draws inside a panel only.

name: workspace
what: Three-region shell: panels, toolbar and viewport list.
render: import { p } from '/app.js'; import { panel } from '/framework/ext/Panel/workspace.js'; panel(() => p('A workspace holds panels'));
notes: A class, not a function; not standalone.

name: doc well (page title block)
what: The title strip at the top of every Doc page.
render: import { div, span, p, a, button, input, textarea, label, details, summary, progress, icon } from '/app.js'; div.c('doc-well', () => div.c('doc-title h2', 'A Doc page title'));
notes: Doc has no exhibit or callout blocks of its own; those live in ext/demo (part B). It only builds tabs, well and files browser.

name: doc files browser
what: A files panel wrapped in .doc-files with panel-height 42em.
undrawable: It is a full panels-based file browser fed by a module url; it needs a whole page frame to lay out.
